newsitem.title: CHINA: YUAN ENDS HIGHER, NEAR 27-MONTH HIGH VS DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: YUAN ENDS HIGHER, NEAR 27-MONTH HIGH VS DOLLAR.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed on Tuesday at 8.2885 to the dollar, near a 27-month high buoyed by speculative buying on expectations of further growth in China's trade surplus, dealers said.
Since the key psychological resistance level of 8.2900 was broken this month, the yuan has shown strong upward momentum despite moves by the central bank to depress the local unit, they said.
"Bidding for the local currency around the 8.2900 level was active today, as China's trade surplus may rise further in July," one dealer said.
The trade figures were expected to be announced later this week, dealers said.
"Although the central bank was seen buying dollars during today's trading, it could only slow the yuan's upward pace rather than reverse the trend," the dealer said.
"One major speculative buy ahead of the close pushed the yuan higher," another dealer said.
It was the highest close since May 17, 1995, when the yuan ended at 8.2805.
However, dealers said they expected the yuan to fall slightly on a technical correction later this week, but further rises were still possible in the short term.

The yuan opened at 8.2897 and quickly touched an intraday low of 8.2948 in early trade. It then moved in a narrow range of 8.2890 to 8.2895 for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2870. The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2896.
It closed up at 7.1310 from 7.1690 against 100 Japanese yen and little changed at 1.0697 from 1.0698 against the Hong Kong dollar.
